narration: Thank God, His people keep growing. Every Sunday, more families fill the church. But with so many faces, it becomes almost impossible to know who came, who is missing, and who quietly drifted away.
Paper lists get lost. And the people who need a call the most are the easiest to miss.
That's where Amoinee comes in. Amoinee, from the Coptic word for "Come!", helps every church know its people, and never lose one of them.

For members, it starts with one simple step, done only once. Create your profile with your name and contact details, and choose whether to turn on face check-in. It's always your choice, and you can turn it off anytime.
At the church door stands the Amoinee kiosk. Just look at the screen as you walk in. In a second it welcomes you by name, and records that you're here.
Prefer not to use your face? No problem. Scan the QR code on the kiosk with your phone, or type the three-digit code of the day. Nobody is ever left at the door.
For Abouna and church servants, Amoinee turns attendance into care.
The Today screen shows who is here, live, as the Liturgy begins, with every arrival time. Weekly events open check-in on their own, so no one has to remember.
The Members page keeps every person in one place, with their photo, consent status, and private notes that only the church's admins can see.

And the Attendance Sheet gives Abouna a clear summary. How many came, who is faithful, who is drifting, and who hasn't come in weeks, ranked from most to least. A beautiful register shows every person at every service, at a glance.

When someone misses several Sundays, Amoinee gently marks them "Follow up needed." Servants add labels like "Called," "Visited," "Needs prayer," or "Traveling," and can snooze a reminder when it's not the right time. Abouna also sees who came back, who is new, and whose birthday is this week.

With one tap, Abouna can print a one-page report, or export everything to Excel. Each church sees only its own people, with access given church by church, and privacy and consent built in from the start.
Because every soul matters, and no one should be forgotten. Amoinee. Come, let us worship.
on-screen text: Every one of God's people, known and cared for.
